ticker: Rupee climbs past 93/USD as investors seek Indian stock shelter
US Senate passes Trump-backed bill making AI data centers pay grid costs
Core sector output growth surges to 10.9% in October
India exposes Pakistani Army's resource grab at United Nations
US religious freedom panel targets India in voter roll revisions

articles.headline: Rupee climbs past 93 against USD
articles.brief: The Indian rupee climbed past 93 per US dollar as investors sought shelter in domestic stocks and shorts unwound. The currency movement comes amid broader global market shifts and robust foreign buying in India's non-AI driven market sectors.

articles.headline: India's AI-free appeal draws record foreign buying
articles.brief: India's stock market continues to draw record foreign inflows due to its distinct AI-free appeal, though corporate earnings will ultimately dictate if the trend lasts. Markets rose for the fourth straight week as global tech routs deepened.

articles.headline: US religious freedom panel targets India voter rolls
articles.brief: The US Commission on International Religious Freedom has claimed that India is deliberately targeting religious minorities during ongoing voter roll revisions. New Delhi has consistently rejected external commentary on its domestic electoral and administrative processes.

articles.headline: Citi underestimated risky assets by $35 billion
articles.brief: Internal sources reveal that banking giant Citi underestimated its risky assets by $35 billion following a series of incorrectly recorded trades. The miscalculation has drawn internal scrutiny regarding risk management protocols and reporting accuracy.

articles.headline: US Senate passes bill for AI data centers grid costs
articles.brief: The US Senate has passed a landmark energy bill requiring large AI data centers to cover more of their local electricity grid upgrade expenses. Lawmakers hope the legislation will mitigate rising consumer utility costs driven by tech expansion.

articles.headline: India exposes Pakistani Army's resource grab at UN
articles.brief: India used the United Nations platform to expose the Pakistani Army's exploitation of mineral wealth for personal and institutional gain. New Delhi linked these ambitions directly to internal political turmoil, regional insurgencies, and economic marginalization.

articles.headline: India develops first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine
articles.brief: India has launched its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, priced affordably at one to two rupees per dose. The government stated the rollout will help curb poultry losses from recurring outbreaks and enhance national disease preparedness.

articles.headline: FDA sets up post-market review council for therapies
articles.brief: The US Food and Drug Administration has established a new council focused on the post-market review of advanced vaccines and gene therapies. The initiative is intended to boost accountability and regulatory transparency for increasingly complex biological products.

articles.headline: Canada lists Goldy Brar as most-wanted criminal
articles.brief: The National Investigation Agency welcomed Canada naming gangster Satinderjeet Singh, alias Goldy Brar, as a most-wanted criminal following a murder investigation. Canadian authorities have announced a significant bounty to secure his capture.

articles.headline: PM Modi delivers civilisational dialogue message at SCO
articles.brief: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, emphasizing dialogue on civilization rather than military conflict. His remarks stressed regional cooperation, economic stability, and shared security challenges.

articles.headline: Core sector output growth jumps to 10.9% in October
articles.brief: India's core sector output growth experienced a sharp acceleration, jumping to 10.9% in October. The robust performance was driven by significant gains in key industrial production indices and infrastructure development projects across the country.

articles.headline: Magnus Carlsen forfeit controversy divides chess world
articles.brief: Grandmaster Magnus Carlsen's decision to forfeit two rapid games against Vladislav Artemiev has sparked fierce debate across the chess community. Top international grandmasters have expressed varied stances, pointing to tournament rule loopholes and calling for reform.

articles.headline: India boycotts Blind Asia Cup trophy ceremony
articles.brief: The Indian cricket team boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup after Pakistan was awarded the title following a rain-abandoned final. The Indian association termed the decision unfair and unilateral.

articles.headline: Anthropic gears up for major stock market debut
articles.brief: Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic is preparing for its highly anticipated stock market debut, drawing intense interest from global retail and institutional investors. Market analysts have issued warnings regarding high volatility and leveraged ETF options.
